intro.title: Amplified AI Accelerator
intro.sub: Eight weeks of installing finished, real estate workflows in your own business, with your operator beside you.
how: Every week has one operating question, one flagship skill from the Library and one required output.
You get the finished skill ahead of time. Live building means setting it up, testing it and putting it to work.
“Working at the end of class” and “implemented by week’s end” aren’t the same thing. We track both.
The rest of the Library stays open the whole time. This week’s skills are just the ones in the spotlight.

roles.owner: Comes to the build, makes the business decisions, approves one real run each week and protects a weekly operating review.
roles.operator: Maintains the workflows: refreshes inputs, reruns outputs, finds failures and follows the repair steps. An owner can hold both roles, on purpose.

intro.scope: No private coaching calls, no custom integrations, no bookkeeping cleanup and no full database cleanup. Those are outside the program.
intro.holiday: Holiday break: no sessions on Dec 23 or Dec 30. No new build until Jan 6.

weeks.title: Get Ready
weeks.question: Are we ready to start on our own data?
why: Week 1 goes fastest when your accounts work, your operator is named and your data is in one place.
None of this is hard. It just has to happen before Dec 2, not during the first build.
weeks.owner: Name your operator, fill in the intake and set up your own AI Brain. Protect a weekly time for the operating review.
weeks.operator: Check access, gather the data pack, set up the working folder and run the readiness exercise.

time.operator: About 2 to 3 hours, when your data is easy to reach.

weeks.title: Know the Business
weeks.question: What are we paying for leads, and what can we trust?
why: Before you change spend or push agents, you need to tell production, revenue, acquisition cost, contribution and data uncertainty apart.
We start with checked spend and lead counts, then go only as far as the data supports.
weeks.owner: Review the exceptions at a fixed weekly time. Decide what you can conclude, what you can’t yet, and what you’d need to know.
weeks.operator: Refresh the weekly numbers view and fill in the worksheet. Refresh source economics monthly, after the books close.

why: The goal isn’t a prettier summary. It’s fewer commitments with nobody’s name on them.

weeks.owner: Review the brief for ten minutes. Accept only tasks with a named owner, a due date and a definition of done.

weeks.question: What should we solve this week?
why: A report is only worth something if it changes a decision or a behavior.

weeks.title: Protect the Pipeline
weeks.question: Where is execution slipping?
why: The point is to send attention to the gaps, not to restate every record in your CRM.
A missing update isn’t the same as a stalled deal. The review has to tell them apart.
weeks.owner: Before your pipeline review, confirm the exceptions with the responsible agents and record a next action for each.
weeks.operator: Run the review before your existing pipeline meeting. Start with active deals and one small priority segment.

weeks.title: Coach from Evidence
weeks.question: What behavior should change for this agent?
why: Missing activity, weak conversion, a bad process and incomplete tracking all look alike on a scorecard. Coaching depends on telling them apart.
AI helps you prepare a better conversation. It doesn’t judge people.
weeks.owner: Before the 1:1, verify the numbers. In it, ask about context, agree on one behavior to change and set the next review date.
weeks.operator: Prepare the packet from agreed activity definitions, production context, prior commitments and the agent’s own perspective.

weeks.title: Delegate an Outcome
weeks.question: What work can leave the owner’s desk without lowering standards?
why: A task that says “handle this” doesn’t define quality or who decides.
AI can draft the work. A person still owns the result and knows when to escalate.

weeks.operator: Run it, or hand it to the team member who now owns it. Check the draft and submit it through your existing approval process.

rubric.meets: Solves a named operating problem and informs an action.

rubric.label: Evidence Quality
rubric.meets: Required facts trace to inputs. Missing information is visible.

rubric.label: Output Quality
rubric.meets: Meets your team’s actual acceptance standard.

rubric.label: Control
rubric.meets: Human approval, access limits and safe failure are explicit.

rubric.label: Repeatability
rubric.meets: A named maintainer can rerun it at the agreed trigger.

rubricRules: Tested: 8 or more out of 10, with no zero in Evidence Quality or Control.
Adopted: tested, plus this week’s use evidence. No score stands in for actual use.

readiness.text: Accounts work, permissions are confirmed, your operator is named and the minimum data is there. Build on your own data.
Accounts work, but a data gap remains. Build on the practice set while a named person fixes the gap, then rerun on your real data. Until you do, the week shows “data repair required.”
No authorized access, no maintainer, or no time to implement. Sort it out before the start, or defer. Don’t let it become an open-ended support problem.

paths.label: Core Path
paths.text: The preconfigured skill, an annotated input example, a minimum-data build, and one reviewed real-world use.

paths.label: Advanced Path
paths.text: The same outcome, plus a harder reconciliation, an edge-case test or a safely scoped connection. Not a second curriculum.

paths.label: Owner Requirement
paths.text: Explain one financial or operating conclusion and approve an action. Your operator can’t do this part for you.

paths.label: Operator Requirement
paths.text: Refresh the input, reproduce an output, find a failure and follow the repair steps.

shared.missedAWeek: Missed a week? Do the core path first: the preconfigured skill, the minimum-data build and one reviewed real use. Extras can wait.

before.practiceSetNote: The practice set is synthetic. The numbers are made up for practice and aren’t a benchmark. One input is missing on purpose, so you can see the worksheet say “unknown” instead of $0.
safeSharing: Redact client and employee details before anything leaves your private folder.
Never upload tax IDs, bank details, identity documents, full transaction files or unrelated personnel records.
Keep your originals. Send the program only redacted evidence.
Keep the cohort’s peer-sharing folder free of client and employee information.
Use one approved AI workspace, and check its data settings before you use live client or employee information.
Drafts by default. Sending, publishing, merging records or writing to your CRM needs a person to approve it.
We won’t use your testimonial, logo, screenshot, numbers or recording publicly without your specific permission.

lanes.label: Connected
lanes.text: An authorized connector you’ve tested. Start read-only. Turn on writes only where a person reviews them.

lanes.label: Exported
lanes.text: CSV or Excel reports and controlled uploads. The default, and a perfectly good finished build.

lanes.label: Manual Minimum
lanes.text: A checked form or a small extract. Same standards. Just don’t call it automated.

graduation: Four core routines in use, each with at least three real cycles: daily prioritization, the weekly numbers review, weekly decision-to-task follow-through and the pipeline exception review.
One checked economics review: a completed baseline, a documented data-quality check, and at least one source decision or a justified decision to collect more data.
One coaching example and one delegation example, in real use with a team member.
One skill you adapted on your own that passes the three tests: a normal case, a missing-information case and a failure case.
One handoff and a 90-day plan: a maintainer other than the instructor, refresh instructions and fallback steps.
after.graduationNote: This is an operating standard, not a promise about results. Attendance and implementation are reported separately. You can come to every session and still be “not yet implemented,” and that’s useful to know.

paths.label: Lead It Yourselves
paths.text: Leave with a 30-day internal rollout plan, the pilot skill, a practice agenda and a scorecard. It’s a real option, and it works without buying anything else.

paths.label: Get Guided Help
paths.text: The Amplified Agent Plan or the Amplified Team Plan runs practice and feedback with your agents. Ask us about the next intake. Any later charges are spelled out before you decide.

paths.label: Defer
paths.text: Keep your owner routines running and revisit agent rollout after you’ve fixed capacity, quality or data issues.

after.noPaywall: No surprise paywall and no automatic enrollment. Your workflows keep working without any future purchase, and your program isn’t incomplete without one.
